args.sql:
SELECT 
    t1.primdx AS diagnosis_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t3.patref) AS number_of_patients,
    SUM(t2.crisisint) AS crisis_rate
FROM 
    assessmentsocialanddiagnosis AS t1
JOIN 
    encounters AS t3 ON t1.asdkey = t3.abref
JOIN 
    treatmentbasics AS t2 ON t3.enckey = t2.encref
GROUP BY 
    t1.primdx
ORDER BY 
    crisis_rate DESC
LIMIT 100;

args.sql:
SELECT 
    t1.primdx AS diagnosis_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t3.patref) AS number_of_patients,
    SUM(t2.crisisint) AS crisis_rate
FROM 
    assessmentsocialanddiagnosis AS t1
JOIN 
    encounters AS t3 ON t1.asdkey = t3.abref
JOIN 
    treatmentbasics AS t2 ON t3.enckey = t2.encref
GROUP BY 
    t1.primdx
ORDER BY 
    crisis_rate DESC
LIMIT 100;

parts.text:
Here are the top 5 diagnoses with the highest crisis rates:

| Diagnosis Name | Number of Patients | Crisis Rate |
|---|---|---|
| PTSD | 220 | 560 |
| Schizophrenia | 201 | 514 |
| Anxiety | 198 | 474 |
| Bipolar | 199 | 466 |
| Depression | 181 | 431 |

The 'assessmentsocialanddiagnosis' table contains the primary diagnosis of each patient. I joined this table with the 'treatmentbasics' table via the 'encounters' table to get the number of crisis interventions for each patient. I then grouped the results by diagnosis, counted the distinct number of patients for each diagnosis, and summed the crisis interventions for each diagnosis. The results are ordered by crisis rate in descending order.
